pairs.fullEnglish: יְיָ was revealed to him in the plains of מַמְרֵא, while he was sitting at the entrance of the tent in the heat of the day.
He raised his eyes and saw, and behold, three men were standing near him. He saw them and ran from the entrance of the tent to meet them, and bowed to the ground.
‘Let them bring a little water now; wash your feet and recline beneath the tree.’
‘I will bring a piece of bread, and you shall strengthen your hearts; afterward you may go on, for this is why you have passed by your servant.’ They said, ‘Do so, as you have spoken.’
Abraham hurried to the tent, to Sarah, and said, ‘Quickly, three seahs of fine flour! Knead it and make cakes.’
Abraham ran to the cattle, took a tender and good calf, and gave it to the young man, who hurried to prepare it.
They said to him, ‘Where is Sarah your wife?’ He said, ‘There, in the tent.’
Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in days; Sarah had ceased to have the way of women.
Sarah laughed within herself, saying, ‘After I have grown old, has youth come to me, when my master is old?’
יְיָ said to Abraham, ‘Why is it that Sarah laughed, saying, “Shall I really, in truth, give birth, when I have grown old?”’
Sarah denied it, saying, ‘I did not laugh,’ for she was afraid. He said, ‘No; rather, you did laugh.’
The men arose from there and looked toward Sodom, and Abraham was walking with them to accompany them.
יְיָ said, ‘Am I concealing from Abraham what I am doing?’
‘Abraham will surely become a numerous and powerful people, and all the peoples of the earth will be blessed on his account.’
יְיָ said, ‘The outcry concerning Sodom and עֲמוֹרָה is indeed great, and their sin is indeed exceedingly grave.’

‘I will now be revealed and judge: if they have acted according to the outcry concerning them that has come up before Me, I will make an end of them (if they do not repent); but if they repent, I will not exact punishment.’
The men turned from there and went to Sodom, while Abraham was still serving in prayer before יְיָ.
Abraham drew near and said, ‘Will You, in anger, destroy the innocent with the guilty?’
‘Perhaps there are fifty innocent people within the city. Will You, in anger, destroy it and not spare the place on account of the fifty innocent people within it?’
יְיָ said, ‘If I find in Sodom fifty innocent people within the city, I will spare the whole place on their account.’
Abraham answered and said, ‘Behold, I have now begun to speak before יְיָ, though I am dust and ashes.’
‘Perhaps the fifty innocent people will lack five. Will You destroy the whole city because of five?’ He said, ‘I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.’
He continued yet again to speak before Him and said, ‘Perhaps forty will be found there.’ He said, ‘I will not make an end of it on account of forty.’
He said, ‘Behold, I have now begun to speak before יְיָ. Perhaps twenty will be found there.’ He said, ‘I will not destroy it on account of twenty.’
The glory of יְיָ withdrew when He finished speaking with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.
The two angels entered Sodom in the evening, while Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. Lot saw them, rose to meet them, and bowed with his face to the ground.

He said, ‘Please, now, my lords, turn aside now to your servant’s house, spend the night, and wash your feet; then you can rise early and go on your way.’ They said, ‘No; rather, we will spend the night in the square.’
He pressed them very strongly, and they turned aside to him and entered his house. He made them a feast and baked unleavened bread for them, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, from young to old, all the people from its farthest extent.
Lot went out to them at the entrance and shut the door behind him.
He said, ‘Please, now, my brothers, do not act wickedly.’

They said, ‘Move farther away!’ And they said, ‘One man came to reside here, and behold, he is passing judgment! Now we will do worse to you than to them.’ They pressed very hard against the man, against Lot, and drew near to break the door.
The men stretched out their hands and brought Lot in to them, into the house, and shut the door.
They struck the men who were at the entrance of the house with blindness, from small to great, and they wearied themselves trying to find the entrance.
The men said to Lot, ‘Who else do you have here? A son-in-law, your sons and your daughters, and everyone belonging to you in the city—bring them out of the place.’
‘For we are destroying this place, because the outcry concerning them has become great before יְיָ, and יְיָ has sent us to destroy it.’
As dawn was rising, the angels urged Lot, saying, ‘Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who have been found faithful with you, lest you be struck on account of the city’s sins.’
He delayed, and the men seized his hand, his wife’s hand, and the hands of his two daughters, because יְיָ had compassion on him. They brought him out and set him down outside the city.
When they had brought them outside, he said, ‘Have pity on your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stop anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountain, lest you be struck.’
‘Behold, now, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is small. Let me escape there now—is it not small?—and my life will be preserved.’
He said to him, ‘Behold, I have accepted your plea in this matter also, not to overturn the city concerning which you have petitioned.’
‘Hurry to escape there, for I cannot do anything until you arrive there.’ Therefore he called the city’s name צוֹעַר.
The sun had risen over the earth when Lot entered צוֹעַר.
יְיָ rained sulfur and fire upon Sodom and upon עֲמוֹרָה, from before יְיָ, from heaven.
He overturned those cities and the whole plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and the vegetation of the ground.
His wife looked from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham rose early in the morning and went to the place where he had served in prayer before יְיָ.
He looked toward Sodom and עֲמוֹרָה and over the whole face of the land of the plain, and saw that, behold, the smoke of the land was rising like the smoke of a furnace.
When יְיָ destroyed the cities of the plain, יְיָ remembered Abraham and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when He overturned the cities in which Lot had been living.
Lot went up from צוֹעַר and lived in the mountain, and his two daughters were with him, for he was afraid to live in צוֹעַר. He lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.
The older said to the younger, ‘Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to come in to us in the way of all the earth.’
‘Come, let us give our father wine to drink and lie with him, and establish children from our father.’
They gave their father wine to drink that night, and the older went in and lay with her father. He did not know when she lay down or when she arose.

On the following day, the older said to the younger, ‘Behold, I lay with Father last night. Let us give him wine to drink tonight also, and you go in and lie with him, and let us establish children from our father.’
They gave their father wine to drink that night also, and the younger arose and lay with him. He did not know when she lay down or when she arose.
Lot’s two daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older gave birth to a son and called his name מוֹאָב; he is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger also gave birth to a son and called his name בַּר עַמִּי; he is the father of the children of עַמּוֹן to this day.
Abraham journeyed from there to the land of the south and lived between רְקָם and חַגְרָא, and resided in גְרָר.
Abraham said concerning Sarah his wife, ‘She is my sister.’ אֲבִימֶלֶךְ, king of גְרָר, sent and took Sarah.
A word from before יְיָ came to אֲבִימֶלֶךְ in a dream of the night and said to him, ‘Behold, you are to die because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man’s wife.’
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ had not approached her, and he said, ‘יְיָ, will You kill even an innocent people?’
‘Did he not say to me, “She is my sister”? And she herself also said, “He is my brother.” In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.’

The word from before יְיָ said to him in the dream, ‘It is also revealed before Me that you did this in the integrity of your heart. I, too, prevented you from sinning before Me; therefore I did not allow you to approach her.’
‘Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you will surely die, you and everyone belonging to you.’
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ rose early in the morning, called all his servants, and spoke all these matters before them; the men were very afraid.

אֲבִימֶלֶךְ called Abraham and said to him, ‘What have you done to us, and what wrong have I done you, that you have brought a great sin upon me and upon my kingdom? You have done to me deeds that are not fit to be done.’
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ said to Abraham, ‘What did you see, that you did this thing?’
Abraham said, ‘Because I said, “Surely there is no fear of יְיָ in this place, and they will kill me on account of my wife.”’
‘But in truth she is my sister, the daughter of my father, though not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.’

‘When the peoples went astray after the works of their hands, יְיָ brought me near to His worship from my father’s house. I said to her, “This is the kindness you shall do for me: in every place to which we go, say concerning me, ‘He is my brother.’”’
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ took sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham; he returned Sarah his wife to him.
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ said, ‘Behold, my land is before you; dwell where it seems right in your eyes.’
For יְיָ had firmly closed every opening of childbirth in the household of אֲבִימֶלֶךְ on account of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
יְיָ remembered Sarah as He had said, and יְיָ did for Sarah as He had spoken.
Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time of which יְיָ had spoken to him.
Abraham called the name of his son who had been born to him, whom Sarah had borne him, Isaac.
Abraham circumcised Isaac his son when he was eight days old, as יְיָ had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him.
Sarah said, ‘יְיָ has made joy for me; everyone who hears will rejoice for me.’
The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
She said to Abraham, ‘Drive out this female servant and her son, for the son of this female servant shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac.’
The matter was very grievous in Abraham’s eyes on account of his son.

יְיָ said to Abraham, ‘Let it not be grievous in your eyes concerning the youth and concerning your female servant. Whatever Sarah says to you, accept it from her, for through Isaac children will be called yours.’
‘And I will also make the female servant’s son into a people, for he is your son.’
The water in the skin was exhausted, and she cast the child beneath one of the trees.
She went and sat down opposite him, keeping her distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, ‘Let me not see the child’s death.’ She sat opposite him, raised her voice, and wept.

The child’s voice was heard before יְיָ, and the angel of יְיָ called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, ‘What is the matter with you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for the child’s voice has been heard before יְיָ in the place where he is.’
‘Arise, lift up the child and take a firm hold of him with your hand, for I will make him into a numerous people.’
יְיָ uncovered her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the skin with water and gave the child to drink.
The Word of יְיָ was in support of the child, and he grew, lived in the wilderness, and became a bowman.
He lived in the wilderness of פָּארָן, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time אֲבִימֶלֶךְ and פִּיכֹל, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, ‘The Word of יְיָ is in your support in everything you do.’

‘Now swear to me here by the Word of יְיָ that you will not deal falsely with me, with my son, or with my son’s son. According to the kindness I have shown you, you shall act toward me and toward the land in which you have resided.’
Abraham said, ‘I will swear.’
Abraham reproved אֲבִימֶלֶךְ concerning the well of water that the servants of אֲבִימֶלֶךְ had seized by force.
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ said, ‘I do not know who did this thing. You yourself did not tell me, and I myself did not hear of it until today.’
Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to אֲבִימֶלֶךְ, and the two of them made a covenant.
Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock apart by themselves.
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ said to Abraham, ‘What are these seven ewe lambs that you have set apart by themselves?’
He said, ‘You shall accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand, so that it may be testimony for me that I dug this well.’
Therefore he called that place בְּאֵר שָׁבַע, for there the two of them swore.
They made a covenant at בְּאֵר שָׁבַע. אֲבִימֶלֶךְ and פִּיכֹל, the commander of his army, arose and returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for many days.
After these things, יְיָ tested Abraham and said to him, ‘Abraham!’ He said, ‘Here I am.’
He said, ‘Take now your son, your only one, whom you love, Isaac, and go to the land of worship. Offer him up there before Me as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will tell you.’

Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took his two young men with him and Isaac his son. He split wood for the burnt offering, arose, and went to the place of which יְיָ had told him.
On the third day Abraham raised his eyes and saw the place from afar.
Abraham said to his young men, ‘Wait here with the donkey, while I and the youth go as far as there; we will bow down and return to you.’
Isaac spoke to Abraham his father and said, ‘Father!’ He said, ‘Here I am, my son.’ He said, ‘Behold, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?’
They came to the place of which יְיָ had told him. Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood, bound Isaac his son, and placed him on the altar above the wood.
Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
The angel of יְיָ called to him from heaven and said, ‘Abraham, Abraham!’ He said, ‘Here I am.’

After these things Abraham raised his eyes and saw, and behold, a ram was behind him, caught in a tree by its horns. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham worshiped and prayed there, in that place, and said before יְיָ, ‘Here the generations shall worship.’ Therefore it will be said on this day, ‘On this mountain Abraham worshiped before יְיָ.’
The angel of יְיָ called to Abraham a second time from heaven.
He said, ‘By My Word I have sworn, says יְיָ: because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son, your only one,’
‘I will surely bless you and greatly multiply your children like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. Your children shall inherit the cities of their enemies.’
‘All the peoples of the earth shall be blessed on account of your children, because you have obeyed My Word.’
Abraham returned to his young men, and they arose and went together to בְּאֵר שָׁבַע. Abraham lived in בְּאֵר שָׁבַע.
After these things it was reported to Abraham, saying, ‘Behold, מִלְכָּה, she too has borne children to נָחוֹר your brother:’
‘עוּץ his firstborn, בּוּז his brother, and קְמוּאֵל the father of אֲרָם,’
‘and כֶּשֶׂד, חֲזוֹ, פִּלְדָּשׁ, יִדְלָף, and בְּתוּאֵל.’
בְּתוּאֵל fathered רִבְקָה. These eight מִלְכָּה bore to נָחוֹר, Abraham’s brother.
His concubine, whose name was רְאוּמָה, also bore טֶבַח, גַּחַם, תַּחַשׁ, and מַעֲכָה.
He said, ‘יְיָ, if I have now found favor before You, please do not pass away from Your servant.’

qualifications.he: הגוף מתרגם את הנוסח הראשי קֳדָמָךְ: לפניך. החילוף המסופק בְּעֵינָיךְ פירושו בעיניך. הפנייה יְיָ נשמרת כפי שהיא בנוסח המסופק.
qualifications.en: The body follows the main קֳדָמָךְ, ‘before You.’ The supplied alternative בְּעֵינָיךְ means ‘in Your eyes.’ The address יְיָ is retained as supplied.

pairs.fullEnglish: He took dairy fat and milk and the calf that he had prepared, and set them before them. He attended to them beneath the tree, and they ate.

qualifications.he: המילה מציינת שומן; התרגום שומן חלב נשען על הקשרה לצד חלב בארוחה. הנוסח אינו מכריע כאן אם מדובר בחמאה דווקא, בשמנת או במוצר שומן חלב אחר, ואין בתרגום קביעה של אופן הכנת המוצר.
qualifications.en: The word denotes fat; ‘dairy fat’ reflects its setting beside milk in the meal. This wording does not decide between butter, cream or another milk-fat product, or assert a particular method of preparation.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, ‘I will surely return to you at a time like this, while you are still living, and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.’ Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, which was behind him.

qualifications.he: כְּעִדָּן משמר השוואה בזמן, ואילו דְּאַתּוּן קַיָּמִין מדבר אל נמענים ברבים בלשון קיום בחיים. האנגלית משמרת זמן כזה והיותם בחיים; היא אינה מוסיפה שנה הבאה או תאריך שהמילים המסופקות אינן מציינות במפורש.
qualifications.en: כְּעִדָּן expresses a comparison of time, and דְּאַתּוּן קַיָּמִין addresses a plural ‘you’ in terms of being alive. The English retains both a time like this and their continuing life; it does not insert ‘next year’ or an expressly stated date absent from these supplied words.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Can a matter be hidden from before יְיָ? At the appointed time I will return to you, at a time like this, while you are still living, and Sarah will have a son.’

qualifications.he: התרגום משמר הן את השוואת הזמן שבכְּעִדָּן הן את לשון הקיום בחיים שבדְּאַתּוּן קַיָּמִין. אַתּוּן הוא פנייה ברבים. שנה הבאה אינה מפורשת במילים אלה, ואין היא נוספת כאן.
qualifications.en: The English retains both the comparison of time in כְּעִדָּן and the language of continuing life in דְּאַתּוּן קַיָּמִין. אַתּוּן is plural. These words do not expressly say ‘next year,’ and that phrase has not been added.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘For it is revealed before Me, since he will command his children and the people of his household after him; and they will keep the ways that are right before יְיָ, doing righteousness and justice, so that יְיָ may bring upon Abraham what He has spoken concerning him.’

qualifications.he: הנוסח הראשי אומר כי גלוי לפניי, בלי מושא מפורש, והתרגום אינו משלים כאן ידעתיו. בְּדִיל דִּי מתורגם בקשר סיבתי: מפני שיצווה; הוא עשוי להתפרש גם בקשר תכלית: כדי שיצווה. החילוף המסופק יְדַעְתִּנֵיהּ אומר ידעתיו והוא קריאה נבדלת, שלא הוחלפה בנוסח הראשי.
qualifications.en: The main reading says ‘it is revealed before Me’ without an expressed object; the English does not turn that into ‘I have known him.’ בְּדִיל דִּי is rendered causally, ‘since he will command’; it can also introduce purpose, ‘so that he may command.’ The supplied יְדַעְתִּנֵיהּ means ‘I have known him’ and remains a distinct alternative, not a substitution for the main text.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Your judgments are true and exclude such an act: killing the innocent with the guilty, so that the innocent should be like the guilty. Your judgments are true! Shall the One who judges all the earth not do justice?’

qualifications.he: המילים דיניך אמת חוזרות פעמיים. מִלְּמֶעְבַּד מובן כאן כלשון הרחקה מן המעשה המתואר, ולא הוחלף בנוסח חלילה לך. בסיום, הגוף קורא את דְּדָיִן ... לָא כשאלת תמיהה בשלילה. החילוף הֲדַיַן מציג את השופט בלשון שאלה; החילוף בְּרַם במקום לָא מביע אישור: אכן יעשה משפט. החילופים אינם מצורפים לנוסח ראשי חדש.
qualifications.en: ‘Your judgments are true’ occurs twice. מִלְּמֶעְבַּד is taken restrictively, excluding the described act, rather than being replaced by ‘far be it from You.’ At the end the body reads דְּדָיִן ... לָא as a negative rhetorical question. The alternative הֲדַיַן presents ‘the Judge’ interrogatively; בְּרַם in place of לָא gives affirmation, ‘will indeed do justice.’ The alternatives have not been combined into a new main text.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, ‘Please let anger not now grow strong before יְיָ, and I will speak. Perhaps thirty will be found there.’ He said, ‘I will not make an end of it if I find thirty there.’

qualifications.he: המילה כעס מושלמת באנגלית כנושא המובן מן הבקשה; אין בנוסח הראשי שם עצם מפורש במקום זה. הפנייה נשארת לפני יְיָ, ואין היא תיאור גופני. רוּגְזָא, המופיעה כחילוף מסופק אחרי קֳדָם, פירושה כעס; החילוף אינו מוחלף בשקט בנוסח הראשי, ואין כאן שחזור של היקף החלפתו.
qualifications.en: ‘Anger’ is supplied as the subject understood from the petition; no corresponding noun is explicit in the main reading here. The expression remains ‘before יְיָ,’ not a bodily description. רוּגְזָא, supplied as an alternative after קֳדָם, means ‘anger’; its precise replacement span is not reconstructed, and it has not silently replaced the main text.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, ‘Please let anger not now grow strong before יְיָ, and I will speak only this once. Perhaps ten will be found there.’ He said, ‘I will not destroy it on account of ten.’

qualifications.he: כעס הוא נושא מושלם באנגלית לפי משמעות הבקשה, לא מילה מפורשת בפסוק. לשון יִתְקֹף נשמרת כיתגבר, והבקשה נותרת לפני יְיָ; אין בתרגום טענה שנכתב כאן שם עצם המציין כעס.
qualifications.en: ‘Anger’ is supplied from the petition's meaning, not translated from an explicit noun in this verse. ‘Grow strong’ retains יִתְקֹף, and the petition remains ‘before יְיָ’; the English does not imply that the source expressly contains a noun for anger.

pairs.fullEnglish: They called to Lot and said to him, ‘Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, so that we may know them.’

qualifications.he: לדעת אותם משמש כאן לשון נקייה ליחסי מין, כפי שעולה גם מהצעת לוט בפסוק ח. אין זו בקשה להיכרות או למסירת מידע על האורחים.
qualifications.en: ‘Know them’ is a euphemism for sexual intercourse here, as Lot's response in verse 8 also indicates. The demand is not a request for acquaintance or information about the guests.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Behold, now, I have two daughters whom no man has known. Let me bring them out to you now, and do to them as seems right in your eyes. Only do nothing to these men, for this is why they have entered beneath the shelter of my roof.’

qualifications.he: גְּבַר הוא האיש שלא ידע את הבנות; הן המושא של יְדָעִנּוּן. הידיעה היא לשון נקייה ליחסי מין, ולא ידיעה שכלית או היכרות רגילה.
qualifications.en: גְּבַר is the man who has not known the daughters; they are the object of יְדָעִנּוּן. ‘Known’ is a sexual euphemism, not intellectual knowledge or ordinary acquaintance.

pairs.fullEnglish: Lot went out and spoke with his sons-in-law, the men taking his daughters, and said, ‘Arise, leave this place, for יְיָ is destroying the city.’ But in his sons-in-law’s eyes he was like one joking.

qualifications.he: הנוסח מכנה אותם חתניו ומוסיף תיאור משתתף: לוקחי בנותיו לנשים. צורת הביטוי כשלעצמה אינה מכריעה אם הנישואין כבר הושלמו או עומדים להתקיים; התרגום אינו מחליף אותה בקביעה בלעדית של נשואים או מאורסים.
qualifications.en: The source calls them his sons-in-law and describes them participially as the men taking his daughters as wives. That expression by itself does not settle whether the marriages were completed or prospective; the English does not replace it with an exclusive assertion of either already married or merely betrothed status.

pairs.fullEnglish: Lot said to them, ‘Please, now, my lords!’

qualifications.he: הנוסח הראשי פונה לאדונים, והפסוק פותח בלָהֶם במשמעות לְהוֹן. החילוף המסופק יְיָ הוא פנייה נבדלת ואין למזג את שתי הקריאות. בפסוק הבא באות צורות נוכח יחיד; הן אינן מתוקנות כאן לרבים ואין נקבעת על פיהן זהות חדשה לדובר או לנמען. לא נוספה מילת שלילה שאינה בנוסח המסופק.
qualifications.en: The main reading addresses lords and begins ‘to them.’ The supplied יְיָ is a distinct alternative address, not a reading to merge into it. The following verse uses singular second-person forms; these have not been changed to plural or used to invent a new speaker or addressee. No negative absent from the supplied text has been inserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Behold, now, your servant has found favor before you, and you have made great the kindness you have shown me by preserving my life. But I am unable to escape to the mountain, lest disaster overtake me and I die.’

qualifications.he: הפנייה בפסוק זה היא לנוכח יחיד, וכן בצורות וְאַסְגֵּיתָא וטֵיבוּתָךְ. האנגלית you אינה מבחינה במספר; אין בכך שינוי לרבים או הכרעה בזהות הנמען מעבר ללשון המסופקת.
qualifications.en: This verse addresses a singular ‘you,’ also expressed in וְאַסְגֵּיתָא and טֵיבוּתָךְ. English ‘you’ does not show number; it does not change the source to plural or determine the addressee's identity beyond the supplied wording.

pairs.fullEnglish: Abraham prayed before יְיָ, and יְיָ healed אֲבִימֶלֶךְ, his wife, and his female servants, and they were relieved.

qualifications.he: המילה מביעה רווחה או הקלה. הפסוק הבא מפרט עצירת פתחי לידה בבית המלך; כאן נשמרת לשון ההקלה, בלי להוסיף שכל הנזכרים ילדו או שהפסוק מונה פתחים גופניים אחרים.
qualifications.en: The word expresses relief. The following verse specifies closure of the household's childbirth openings; this verse retains the broader relief wording without asserting that everyone named gave birth or adding other bodily passages not listed here.

pairs.fullEnglish: Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, placing them upon her shoulder. He also gave her the child and sent her away. She went and wandered in the wilderness of בְּאֵר שָׁבַע.

qualifications.he: בנוסח בא ואת הילד אחרי הניח על כתפה. התרגום חוזר על נתינה כדי למסור באנגלית שלמה שהילד ניתן להגר, בלי לקבוע שלא הונח על כתפה. החיבור עשוי לכלול את הילד גם בהנחה על הכתף; אפשרות זו נשמרת כאן ואינה נשללת בשל גיל המיוחס לו ממקום אחר.
qualifications.en: The source places ‘and the child’ after ‘placed upon her shoulder.’ The English repeats the giving to express in a complete sentence that the child was given to Hagar; it does not assert that he was not placed on her shoulder. The coordination may include the child in the shoulder placement as well. That possibility remains open and is not excluded by an age inferred from elsewhere.

pairs.fullEnglish: He planted a planting in בְּאֵר שָׁבַע and prayed there in the name of יְיָ, the God of the world.

qualifications.he: הגוף שומר את השם הכללי נטיעה. החילוף המסופק אִילָנָא אומר עץ; אין הוא מחייב להחליף את המילה הראשית או לזהות מין עץ מסוים. אין בתרגום זיהוי של מין הצמח או קביעה שמדובר בריבוי עצים.
qualifications.en: The body retains the general noun ‘a planting.’ The supplied alternative אִילָנָא means ‘a tree’; it has not replaced the main word or supplied a tree species. The English identifies neither a plant species nor a plurality of trees.

pairs.fullEnglish: Abraham said, ‘Before יְיָ, the lamb for the burnt offering is known to Him, my son.’ And the two of them went together.

qualifications.he: הניסוח משמר גם לפני יְיָ וגם את כינוי לֵיהּ, המובן בגוף כלו במובן ידוע לו. הכינוי עשוי לשאת גם גוון של בשבילו או לעצמו; אין מכך תוספת של הבאת השה בפועל. גְּלֵי נשאר ידוע או גלוי, ולא הוחלף בראייה, בהמצאה או בהבטחת אספקה שאינה מפורשת בנוסח.
qualifications.en: The wording retains both ‘before יְיָ’ and לֵיהּ, taking the latter as ‘to Him’ in the knowledge expression. The pronoun can also carry a benefactive force, ‘for Him/for Himself’; neither wording adds an actual bringing of the lamb. גְּלֵי remains known or revealed, not seeing, finding or an expressly promised provision absent from the supplied text.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, ‘Do not stretch out your hand against the youth, and do nothing to him, for now I know that you fear יְיָ, and you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me.’

qualifications.he: הגוף נוקט עתה אני יודע לפי יְדַעְנָא. החילוף המסופק יְדָעִית הוא צורת עבר: ידעתי. הדובר המוצג בפסוק הקודם הוא מלאך יְיָ, ובסוף דבריו נאמר מִנִּי, ממני; התרגום משמר את גוף ראשון ואינו מחליף אותו בשם נמען מפורש.
qualifications.en: The body follows יְדַעְנָא, ‘now I know.’ The supplied יְדָעִית is a past form, ‘I knew/have known.’ The preceding verse introduces the angel of יְיָ as speaker, and this speech ends with מִנִּי, ‘from me’; the first person is retained rather than replaced with an explicitly named referent.

pairs.fullEnglish: Elisha said to her, ‘What shall I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house.’ She said, ‘Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a vessel of oil.’
He said, ‘Go and borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels. Do not get only a few.’
She went away from him and closed the door behind herself and her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she poured out the oil.
When the supply of vessels was exhausted, she said to her son, ‘Bring me another vessel.’ He said to her, ‘There is no other vessel.’ Then the oil stopped.
If you lie down and sleep, you will not be afraid; you will lie down, and your sleep will be pleasant.
For God will be your support, and He will guard your foot so that you are not caught in a snare.
Do not hold back from doing good when it is in your power to act.
Do not say to your fellow, ‘Go and come back, and tomorrow I will give,’ when you have it with you.
Do not plan evil against your fellow while he lives at ease with you.
She came and told the prophet of יְיָ. He said, ‘Go, sell the oil and pay your creditors. You and your sons shall be sustained by what remains.’
One day Elisha passed through Shunem. There was a woman there who feared sin, and she pressed him to eat bread. Whenever he passed through, he would turn aside there to eat bread.
She said to her husband, ‘Look, now I know that he is a holy prophet of יְיָ, who regularly turns aside to us.’
‘Let us now make a small walled upper chamber, and arrange a place for a bed for him there, and a table, a chair, and a lampstand. Then, when he comes to us, he can turn aside there.’
Do not quarrel with a person without cause, if he has done you no harm.
Do not envy a man who seizes by force, and do not desire any of his ways.
God’s curse is in the houses of the wicked, but He will bless the dwelling-place of the righteous.
One day he came there, turned aside to the upper chamber, and lay down there.
He said to Gehazi, his attendant, ‘Call this Shunammite woman.’ He called her, and she stood before him.
He said, ‘Then what can be done for her?’ Gehazi said, ‘In truth, she has no son, and her husband is old.’
He said, ‘Call her.’ He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
The wise will inherit honor, but fools will receive disgrace.
Listen, sons, to a father’s discipline, and pay attention so as to know understanding.
For I have given you good instruction; do not abandon my teaching.
The boy grew. One day he went out to his father, to the reapers.
He said to his father, ‘My head! My head!’ His father said to the attendant, ‘Take him and carry him to his mother.’
He took him and carried him to his mother. The boy sat on her knees until noon, and died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the prophet of יְיָ, closed the door upon him, and went out.
Acquire wisdom; acquire understanding. Do not forget, and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.
The beginning of wisdom is: acquire wisdom; with all your acquiring, acquire understanding.
Cherish her, so that she may raise you high; embrace her, so that she may honor you.
She will place gracious beauty on your head, a crown of splendor upon you.
She called to her husband and said, ‘Please send me one of the attendants and one of the female donkeys. I will make my way to the prophet of יְיָ and return.’
She went and came to the prophet of יְיָ at Mount Carmel. When the prophet of יְיָ saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi, his attendant, ‘Look, there is that Shunammite woman.’
Listen, my son, and receive from me, and the years of your life will increase.
I have taught you the way of wisdom and led you along upright paths.
When you walk, your path will not be constricted; and if you run, you will not stumble.
Hold firmly to discipline and do not slacken. Guard it, for it is your life.
Do not walk in the path of the wicked, and do not envy the way of evil people.
‘Then go in and close the door behind yourself and your son, and pour into all these vessels. Set aside each vessel that becomes full.’

qualifications.he: בנוסח כאן נאמר ‘בנך’ בלשון יחיד; בפסוק הבא נאמר ‘בניה’ בלשון רבים. התרגום משמר את שינוי המספר ואינו משנה את אחד הנוסחים כדי להתאימו לאחר.
qualifications.en: The wording here says ‘your son’ in the singular; the next verse says ‘her sons’ in the plural. The translation preserves that change in number rather than altering either wording to match the other.

pairs.fullEnglish: For I was a son to my father, tenderly cherished and an only son before my mother.

qualifications.he: הדובר מתאר את עצמו כבן מפונק ויחיד לפני אמו. ‘בן יחיד’ משמר את לשון ‘יחידא’ ביחס לאמו; המשפט אינו מונה את כל ילדי אביו ואינו מפרט את תולדות המשפחה.
qualifications.en: The speaker describes himself as tenderly cherished and an only son before his mother. ‘An only son’ preserves the designation ‘יחידא’ in relation to his mother; the sentence does not enumerate all his father's children or supply a family history.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, ‘Why are you going to him today? It is neither the new moon nor Shabbos.’ She said, ‘Peace.’

qualifications.he: ‘שלם’ היא תשובתה המלאה כאן. הנוסח אינו מפרש אם זו הרגעה או חתימת השיחה, ואינו מוסיף הבטחה על מה שיקרה בהמשך.
qualifications.en: ‘שְׁלָם’ is her complete reply here. The wording does not explain whether it reassures or closes the exchange, and it adds no promise about what will happen afterward.

pairs.fullEnglish: For crookedness is kept far from before יְיָ, and His conversation is with the upright.

qualifications.he: ‘שועיתיה’ מציין את שיחו, והישרים הם אלה שעמם השיח. הנוסח אינו מפרט את תוכן השיח ואינו אומר כאן במפורש שנמסר להם סוד או עניין מסוים של התגלות.
qualifications.en: ‘שׁוּעִיתֵיהּ’ denotes His conversation, with the upright as those with whom He converses. The wording does not specify the conversation's content or expressly say here that a secret or a particular revelation is communicated to them.

pairs.fullEnglish: He taught me and said to me, ‘(יְיָ) Let your heart clasp my words; keep my commandments and live.’

qualifications.he: הנוסח כולל את ‘(יְיָ)’ בין ‘ואמר לי’ ובין ‘יקמט’. השם והסוגריים נשמרים במקומם, אך זיקתו התחבירית של השם אינה מפורשת; התרגום אינו מוסיף לו פועל ואינו מחליף את ‘הוא’ בשם של דובר מסוים. ‘יקמט’ מתאר אחיזה וכינוס של הדברים בלב.
qualifications.en: The wording includes ‘(יְיָ)’ between ‘said to me’ and ‘let … clasp.’ The Name and parentheses are retained in place, but the Name's grammatical attachment is not explicit; the translation supplies no verb for it and does not replace ‘He’ with a specifically identified speaker. ‘יְקַמֵט’ conveys holding or gathering the words within the heart.
qualifications.anchor: וְאַלְפַנִי וַאֲמַר לִי (יְיָ) יְקַמֵט מִלַי לִבָּךְ

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Now, run now to meet her, and say to her: Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the boy?’ She said, ‘Peace.’

qualifications.he: השאלות נוגעות לשלום האשה, בעלה והילד; תשובתה היא המילה היחידה ‘שלם’. מאחר שמות הילד כבר סופר, אין לקרוא את מסירת תשובתה כקביעה של המספר שהילד חי, או כהבטחה שיחיה. כוונתה השיחתית אינה מפורשת.
qualifications.en: The questions concern the woman, her husband, and the boy; her reply is the single word ‘שְׁלָם.’ Since the boy's death has already been narrated, reporting her reply is not a statement by the narrator that the boy is alive, nor a promise that he will live. Her conversational intention is not made explicit.
qualifications.anchor: הַשְׁלָם לִיךְ הַשְׁלָם לְבַעֲלִיךְ הַשְׁלָם לְרַבְיָא וַאֲמַרַת שְׁלָם

pairs.fullEnglish: A certain woman, one of the wives of the disciples of the prophets, cried out before Elisha, saying: ‘Your servant Obadiah, my husband, has died. You know that your servant feared before יְיָ. When Jezebel killed the prophets of יְיָ, he took a hundred men from among them and hid them, in groups of fifty men, in a cave. He would borrow and feed them, so as not to feed them from Ahab’s property, because it was acquired by extortion. And now the creditor has come to take my two sons as slaves for himself.’
He will sweep away the scoffers, but to the humble He will give kindness.

qualifications.he: ‘ממקני’ הם המלגלגים. הפועל ‘נסחוף’ מתאר סחיפה או הפלה שלהם, ולא לעג המופנה אליהם בחזרה; מולם עומדים הענווים, שלהם ניתן חסד.
qualifications.en: ‘מְמִקְנֵי’ designates the scoffers. The verb ‘נִסְחוֹף’ describes sweeping them away or overthrowing them, not mocking them in return; the contrasting group is the humble, to whom kindness is given.

pairs.fullEnglish: Do not abandon her, and she will guard you; love her, so that she may choose you.

qualifications.he: הסיום משתמש בלשון גבא, בחירה ולקיחה אליה: החכמה היא הבוחרת באוהב אותה. אין זו חזרה אוטומטית על פועל השמירה ‘ותנטריך’ שבתחילת הפסוק, ואין כאן הבטחה מפורטת לאופן מסוים של הגנה.
qualifications.en: The ending uses the choosing or taking-to-oneself sense of גבא: wisdom is the one who chooses the person who loves her. It is not automatically a repetition of the guarding verb ‘וְתִנְטַרְיָךְ’ at the beginning of the verse, nor does it specify a particular form of protection.

pairs.fullEnglish: To Sarah he said, ‘Behold, I have given a thousand silver sela coins to your brother. Behold, it is for you a covering of honor, in compensation for my having sent and taken you and seen you and all who are with you.’ And concerning everything she had said, she was reproved.

qualifications.he: גוף התרגום הולך אחר כְּסוּת דִּיקָר, כיסוי של כבוד. עַיְנִין שבסוגריים פירושה ׳עיניים׳, והיא קריאה נפרדת ולא תוספת המצורפת לקריאה הראשית. המתנה היא אלף סלעי כסף. שני צירופי יָת שלאחר וַחֲזֵית הם מושאי הראייה: שרה וכל אשר עמה. רש״י מסביר כאן במפורש את לשון אונקלוס: ׳וְעַל כֵּן תִּרְגְּמוֹ וַחֲזֵית יָתִיךְ וְיַת כָּל דְּעִמָּךְ׳. בסיום, דַּאֲמָרַת ואִתּוֹכָחַת מנוקדות כצורות עבר בגוף שלישי נקבה יחידה: על כל מה שאמרה, היא הוּכחה. לפיכך הסיום נמסר כדיווח עליה ולא כהמשך הפנייה אליה בגוף שני. ביאור רש״י ללשון המקרא על פתחון פה ובירור דברים אינו מועתק במקום לשון התרגום.
qualifications.en: The body follows כְּסוּת דִּיקָר, a covering of honor. The parenthetical עַיְנִין means ‘eyes’ and is a separate reading, not an addition combined with the main one. The gift is a thousand silver sela coins. Both יָת phrases following וַחֲזֵית are objects of seeing: Sarah and all who are with her. Rashi explicitly explains this Targum wording: ‘וְעַל כֵּן תִּרְגְּמוֹ וַחֲזֵית יָתִיךְ וְיַת כָּל דְּעִמָּךְ.’ In the ending, דַּאֲמָרַת and אִתּוֹכָחַת are pointed as third-person feminine singular perfect forms: concerning everything she had said, she was reproved. The close is therefore rendered as a report about her, not a continuation of second-person address. Rashi's own explanation of the Biblical Hebrew in terms of a right to argue and clarification is not substituted for the Targum.
qualifications.anchor: הָא הוּא לִיךְ כְּסוּת דִּיקָר (עַיְנִין) חֳלַף דִּשְׁלָחִית דְּבַרְתִּיךְ וַחֲזֵית יָתִיךְ וְיָת כָּל דְּעִמָּךְ וְעַל כָּל מַה דַּאֲמָרַת אִתּוֹכָחַת

pairs.fullEnglish: The woman conceived and bore a son at this season, as at the time when she was alive, as Elisha had spoken with her.

qualifications.he: לְזִמְנָא הָדֵין נמסר ׳למועד הזה׳, והכ״ף של כְּעִדַן נשמרת כהשוואה: ׳כמו בעת שבה הייתה בחיים׳. קַיָמָא נקרא כאן כתיאור קיום וחיים במסגרת לשון הזמן, לא כציון של תנוחת עמידה. רש״י מפרש את כעת חיה העברי ׳כָּעֵת הַזֹּאת שֶׁהָיְתָה בְחַיִּים וּבְשָׁלוֹם׳; ההשוואה תומכת בקריאת החיים, אך המילה ׳בשלום׳ אינה נוספת לגוף הארמי. דְהִיא קַיָמָא נשאר בלשון יחידה, בניגוד לרבים שבביטוי בְּעִדַן דְאַתּוּן קַיָמִין שנמסר בהבטחה. אין משנים את כְּעִדַן לבְּעִדַן, ואין מוסיפים ׳בשנה הבאה׳ או משך היריון שלא נאמרו כאן.
qualifications.en: לְזִמְנָא הָדֵין is ‘at this season,’ and the comparative prefix of כְּעִדַן is retained: ‘as at the time when she was alive.’ קַיָמָא is read here as a state of existing/living within the time expression, not as a statement of standing posture. Rashi explains the Biblical Hebrew כעת חיה as כָּעֵת הַזֹּאת שֶׁהָיְתָה בְחַיִּים וּבְשָׁלוֹם; that comparison supports the life reading, but ‘in peace’ is not added to the Aramaic body. דְהִיא קַיָמָא remains singular, unlike the plural בְּעִדַן דְאַתּוּן קַיָמִין supplied from the promise. כְּעִדַן is not changed into בְּעִדַן, and neither ‘next year’ nor an unstated gestational interval is inserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: She saddled the female donkey and said to her attendant, ‘Drive on and go. Do not hinder me in riding unless I tell you.’

qualifications.he: הצירוף נמסר כאיסור להגביל את הדוברת ברכיבתה: דחק עם עלי מציין לחץ מגביל עליה, ולמרכב מציין את הפעולה הנוגעת לאיסור. הציווי לנהוג וללכת והחריג התלוי בדבריה נשמרים. רש״י על הפסוק העברי מפרש 'אַל תְּעַכֵּב עַל יָדִי אֶת הָרְכִיבָה'; פירוש זה תומך בהבנת ההוראה, אך אינו גלוסה מפורשת למילה הארמית. אין כאן הוראה להאיץ בה כדי שתרכב, ואין קביעה של מהירות, קצב או אופן נהיגה מסוים.
qualifications.en: The combination is rendered as a prohibition on hindering the speaker in her riding: דחק with עלי expresses constraining pressure upon her, and למרכב specifies the activity concerned. The command to drive onward and the exception dependent on her instruction are retained. Rashi on the Hebrew verse explains, 'אַל תְּעַכֵּב עַל יָדִי אֶת הָרְכִיבָה', do not hold up the riding on my account; this corroborates the instruction rather than explicitly glossing the Aramaic word. No command to urge her to ride, or particular speed, pace or driving technique, is asserted.
qualifications.anchor: לָא תִדְחוֹק עֲלַי לְמִרְכַּב אֱלָהֵין כַּד אֵמַר לָךְ

pairs.fullEnglish: He said to him, ‘Now say to her: You have taken all this trouble for us. What is to be done for you? Do you have a matter to discuss with the king or with the commander of the army?’ She said, ‘Within my people's affairs I am supported.’

qualifications.he: מְסוֹבָרָא מתאר את האשה כנתמכת, בלשון נקבה; אין זה פועל פעיל שמשמעו ׳אני מקווה׳ או ׳אני חושבת׳. בְּגוֹ עִסְקֵי עַמִי משאיר את התשובה בתחום ענייני עמה, ולא רק במקום מגורים. התמיכה אינה מפורטת כאן: אין קביעה של קצבה כספית, משרה ציבורית או זהות המסייעים.
qualifications.en: מְסוֹבָרָא describes the woman as supported, with a feminine predicate; it is not an active ‘I hope’ or ‘I think’. בְּגוֹ עִסְקֵי עַמִי places her reply within her people's affairs, not merely at a place of residence. The support is not further specified: no financial allowance, public office or particular supporters are named.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, ‘At this season, at a time when you are alive, you will be embracing a son.’ She said, ‘Please, my master, prophet of יְיָ, let your word not prove false to your maidservant.’

qualifications.he: בְּעִדַן דְאַתּוּן קַיָמִין נמסר כ׳בעת שאתם בחיים׳: אַתּוּן וקַיָמִין בלשון רבים, ואילו ההבטחה תְּהֵא מְחַבְּקָא פונה לאשה ביחידה. לשון הרבים אינה מזהה את שאר הנכללים בפנייה. קַיָמִין מתאר כאן קיום בחיים בתוך ציון הזמן, לא תנוחת עמידה. בארמית לא נאמרו במפורש ׳בשנה הבאה׳, משך היריון או תוספת של בריאות ושלום.
qualifications.en: בְּעִדַן דְאַתּוּן קַיָמִין is rendered ‘at a time when you are alive’: אַתּוּן and קַיָמִין are plural, whereas תְּהֵא מְחַבְּקָא promises the woman's embrace in the feminine singular. The plural does not identify the others included in the address. קַיָמִין here describes living/existing within the time expression, not a standing posture. The Aramaic does not explicitly say ‘next year’, specify a gestational interval or add health and peace.

pairs.fullEnglish: She said, ‘Who is the faithful one who declared to אברהם a promise that שָׂרָה would nurse children? For I have borne a son in his old age.’

qualifications.he: השאלה ׳מי הוא הנאמן׳ נקראת כשבח לנאמנותו של האומר, ולא כהכחשה שניתנה הבטחה. קְיָם הוא שם עצם המציין הבטחה מחייבת, ותוכן ההבטחה בא בדְתוֹנִיק בְּנִין שָׂרָה. אין זו כאן צורת פועל נפרדת האומרת ׳קיים׳. בְּנִין נשאר בלשון רבים, ואילו הלידה שבסוף המשפט היא של בן אחד; אין הוספה של סיפור הנקת ילדים אחרים.
qualifications.en: ‘Who is the faithful one?’ is read as praise of the speaker's faithfulness, not a denial that a promise was made. קְיָם is a noun denoting a binding promise, whose content follows in דְּתוֹנִיק בְּנִין שָׂרָה. It is not here a separate verb saying ‘fulfilled’. בְּנִין remains plural children, whereas the final birth statement concerns one son; the account of nursing other children is not added.

dayTitle.en: Revelation in the Plains of מַמְרֵא and Preparing Hospitality

explanation.he: אונקלוס פותח בלשון התגלות ומעמיד את אברהם בפתח האוהל בחום היום. אברהם רץ לקראת שלושת האנשים ומציע מים, מנוחה ולחם. הוראתו לשרה כוללת כמות מפורשת של שלוש סאין קמח סולת והכנת עוגות.
explanation.en: Onkelos opens with the language of revelation and places Abraham at the tent entrance in the heat of the day. Abraham runs toward the three men and offers water, rest, and bread. His instruction to Sarah specifies three seahs of fine flour and the preparation of cakes.

dayTitle.he: שירות האורחים והבשורה על בן לשרה
dayTitle.en: Serving the Guests and the Announcement of a Son for Sarah

explanation.he: אברהם בוחר בן בקר רך וטוב וממהר להכינו באמצעות הנער. אונקלוס מתאר אותו כמשרת את האורחים מתחת לעץ. שאלתם על שרה מובילה להבטחת השיבה ולבשורה על בן, כאשר שרה שומעת מפתח האוהל.
explanation.en: Abraham selects a tender, good calf and hastens its preparation through the young man. Onkelos describes him as attending to the guests beneath the tree. Their question about Sarah leads to the promise of a return and the announcement of a son, while Sarah listens at the tent entrance.

dayTitle.he: צחוקה של שרה ודבר שאינו נסתר
dayTitle.en: Sarah’s Laughter and a Matter That Is Not Hidden

explanation.he: הזקנה והפסקת אורח הנשים מבהירות את הרקע לצחוקה של שרה. אונקלוס מנסח את התשובה בשאלה אם דבר יכול להתכסות מלפני יְיָ, ולא בשאלה על קושי בביצוע. הבטחת הבן חוזרת, והקטע מסתיים בהכחשת שרה ובתשובה להכחשתה.
explanation.en: Old age and the cessation of the way of women establish the setting for Sarah’s laughter. Onkelos frames the response as a question about whether a matter can be hidden from before יְיָ, rather than a question about difficulty in accomplishing it. The promise of a son is repeated, and the passage ends with Sarah’s denial and the answer to it.

dayTitle.he: דרכי צדקה ומשפט ודין התלוי בתשובה
dayTitle.en: Ways of Righteousness and Justice, and Judgment Conditional on Repentance

explanation.he: הדיבור על אברהם קושר את עתיד עמו לציווי בניו וביתו לשמור דרכים מתוקנות ולעשות צדקה ומשפט. מול זאת מובאת הקבלה על סדום ועמורה וחטאתן החמורה. אונקלוס מנסח את הבירור כהתגלות ודין, ומבחין במפורש בין העדר תשובה לבין תשובה המונעת פירעון.
explanation.en: The speech about Abraham connects his people’s future with his commanding his children and household to keep right ways and practice righteousness and justice. Against this stands the outcry concerning Sodom and עֲמוֹרָה and their grave sin. Onkelos describes the inquiry as revelation and judgment, explicitly distinguishing failure to repent from repentance that prevents punishment.

dayTitle.he: תפילה על החפים ובקשה לחוס על העיר
dayTitle.en: Prayer for the Innocent and a Plea to Spare the City

explanation.he: אונקלוס מתאר את עמידת אברהם כשירות בתפילה לפני יְיָ. שאלותיו מבדילות בין זכאי לחייב ומבקשות שחמישים זכאים יצילו את המקום כולו. התשובה מבטיחה מחילה לכל המקום אם יימצאו בו החמישים.
explanation.en: Onkelos describes Abraham’s remaining there as service in prayer before יְיָ. His questions distinguish the innocent from the guilty and ask that fifty innocent people preserve the whole place. The response promises to spare the entire place if those fifty are found there.

dayTitle.he: מן הבקשה על עשרה אל הוצאת לוט מסדום
dayTitle.en: From the Plea for Ten to Bringing Lot Out of Sodom

explanation.he: אברהם מוסיף לבקש עד לעשרה זכאים, ובסיום הדיבור מסתלק יקר יְיָ. שני המלאכים נכנסים לסדום ומתקבלים בבית לוט, ואנשי העיר מקיפים את הבית. לאחר האזהרה על חורבן המקום, האנשים אוחזים בידי לוט, אשתו ושתי בנותיו ומוציאים אותם, מפני שיְיָ חומל על לוט. לוט מביע חשש שלא יוכל להימלט אל ההר.
explanation.en: Abraham continues his plea down to ten innocent people, and at the close of the speech the glory of יְיָ withdraws. The two angels enter Sodom and are received in Lot's house, which the townsmen surround. After warning of the place's destruction, the men take hold of Lot, his wife and his two daughters and bring them out, because יְיָ has compassion on Lot. Lot expresses fear that he cannot escape to the mountain.

dayTitle.en: Rescue, Covenant, and Trial in the Land of Worship

explanation.he: הקטע עובר מהצלת לוט וחורבן ערי המישור אל בנותיו, וממשיך בדיבור הבא מלפני יְיָ אל אבימלך ובהשבת שרה. לידת יצחק, שמיעת קול הילד של הגר לפני יְיָ וברית הבאר מציגות הבטחה, הצלה והסדרת יחסים; אונקלוס מציין במפורש את מימר יְיָ כסיוע. בניסיון אברהם מודגשים ארץ הפולחן, ידיעת השה לפני יְיָ ותפילת אברהם במקום. הקטע מסתיים בהבטחת ריבוי הבנים ובשמות משפחת נחור.
explanation.en: The passage moves from Lot’s rescue and the overthrow of the plain’s cities to his daughters, then to the word from before יְיָ addressed to אֲבִימֶלֶךְ and Sarah’s return. Isaac’s birth, the hearing of Hagar’s child before יְיָ, and the covenant concerning the well present promise, rescue, and the ordering of relationships; Onkelos explicitly names the Word of יְיָ as support. Abraham’s trial emphasizes the land of worship, the lamb being known before יְיָ, and Abraham’s prayer at the place. The passage closes with the promise of numerous children and the names of נָחוֹר’s family.

dayTitle.he: חוב למען הנביאים ושמן הממלא את הכלים
dayTitle.en: A Debt for the Prophets and Oil That Fills the Vessels

explanation.he: התרגום מזהה את בעל האלמנה כעובדיה ומספר שלווה כדי להאכיל מאה נביאים שהסתיר מפני איזבל, בלי להשתמש ברכוש אחאב שנרכש באונס. אלישע מורה לה לשאול כלים ריקים רבים ולצקת לתוכם מאחורי דלת סגורה. השמן פוסק כאשר אין עוד כלי להביא.
explanation.en: The Targum identifies the widow’s husband as Obadiah and recounts how he borrowed to feed a hundred prophets hidden from Jezebel, rather than use Ahab’s extorted property. Elisha instructs her to borrow many empty vessels and pour into them behind a closed door. The oil stops when there is no further vessel to bring.

dayTitle.he: מנוחה בלא פחד וטובה בלא דיחוי
dayTitle.en: Rest Without Fear and Goodness Without Delay

explanation.he: הקריאה מחברת בין שינה נעימה ובין ביטחון בסעד האל ובשמירתו מפני מלכודת. בצד דברי העידוד היא דורשת שלא להימנע מעשיית טובה כשיש יכולת, ולא לדחות את הזולת למחר כשאפשר לתת כעת. היא חותמת באיסור לתכנן רעה כלפי מי שיושב עמך בשלווה.
explanation.en: The reading links pleasant sleep with confidence in God’s support and protection from a snare. Alongside its encouragement, it calls for doing good when one has the ability and not putting a fellow off until tomorrow when one can give now. It closes by forbidding a plot against someone living at ease with you.

dayTitle.en: Sustenance for the Widow and a Room for the Prophet

explanation.he: האלמנה נשלחת למכור את השמן, לשלם את חובותיה ולהתפרנס עם בניה מן הנותר. לאחר מכן מתוארת אשה בשונם שהתרגום מציין את יראתה מן החטא, והיא מפצירה באלישע לאכול בביתה. בהכירה בו כנביא קדוש היא מבקשת להכין לו חדר עליון ובו מיטה, שולחן, כיסא ומנורה.
explanation.en: The widow is told to sell the oil, pay her debts, and support herself and her sons from what remains. The account then turns to a woman in Shunem whom the Targum describes as fearing sin and who presses Elisha to eat in her home. Recognizing him as a holy prophet, she proposes an upper room furnished with a bed, table, chair, and lampstand.

dayTitle.he: לא לריב חינם ולא לקנא בחוטף
dayTitle.en: Neither Groundless Quarrels nor Envy of the Violent

explanation.he: הפסוקים מזהירים מפני מריבה עם מי שלא עשה רעה ומפני קנאה באדם החוטף בכוח או רצון בדרכיו. התרגום מעמיד את העוול הרחק מלפני יְיָ ואת שיחו עם הישרים. הוא מסיים בניגוד שבין הקללה בבתי הרשעים ובין הברכה למקום מושבם של הצדיקים.
explanation.en: These verses warn against quarreling with someone who has done no harm and against envying a person who seizes by force or desiring his ways. The Targum places crookedness far from before יְיָ and His conversation with the upright. It concludes with the contrast between a curse in the houses of the wicked and blessing for the dwelling-place of the righteous.

dayTitle.en: What Can Be Done for the Hostess?

explanation.he: אלישע משתמש בחדר שהוכן לו ומבקש לקרוא לאשה משונם. הוא מכיר בטרחה שטרחה למענם ומציע לברר אם יש לה עניין אצל המלך או אצל שר הצבא. לאחר תשובתה על מקומה בענייני עמה, גיחזי מציין שאין לה בן ושבעלה זקן, והיא נקראת שוב ועומדת בפתח.
explanation.en: Elisha uses the room prepared for him and asks for the woman from Shunem to be called. He acknowledges the trouble she has taken for them and asks whether she has a matter with the king or the army commander. After her reply concerning her place within her people’s affairs, Gehazi notes that she has no son and that her husband is old; she is called again and stands in the doorway.

dayTitle.en: The Promise of a Son and the Grief That Followed

explanation.he: אלישע מבטיח לאשה שתחבק בן במועד שהוא מציין, והיא מבקשת שדבריו לא יכזבו לה. התרגום מספר על הריונה ולידת הבן ועל גדילתו, עד יציאתו אל אביו ואל הקוצרים. לאחר תלונתו על ראשו הוא נישא לאמו, מת על ברכיה בצהריים, והיא מניחה אותו על מיטת הנביא ויוצאת.
explanation.en: Elisha promises that the woman will embrace a son at the time he specifies, and she asks that his word not prove false to her. The Targum recounts her conception, the son’s birth and growth, and his going out to his father and the reapers. After crying out about his head, he is carried to his mother and dies on her knees at noon; she lays him on the prophet’s bed and goes out.

dayTitle.en: The Journey to the Prophet and the Reply of Peace

explanation.he: האשה מבקשת מבעלה נער ואתון כדי להגיע אל נביא יְיָ ולשוב. לשאלתו מדוע היא הולכת ביום שאינו ראש חודש או שבת היא משיבה במילה ‘שלם’, ומורה לנער כיצד לנהוג בדרך. הנביא רואה אותה מרחוק בהר הכרמל ושולח את גיחזי לשאול לשלומה, לשלום בעלה ולשלום הנער; גם הפעם תשובתה קצרה.
explanation.en: The woman asks her husband for an attendant and a female donkey so that she can reach the prophet of יְיָ and return. When he asks why she is going on a day that is neither the new moon nor Shabbos, she replies ‘Peace’ and gives her attendant directions for the journey. The prophet sees her from a distance at Mount Carmel and sends Gehazi to ask about her, her husband, and the boy; again her reply is brief.

dayTitle.en: Holding Fast to Discipline and Avoiding the Wicked Path

explanation.he: האב מבקש מבנו להקשיב ולקבל ממנו, ומקשר זאת לריבוי שנות חייו. הוא מתאר את הוראת החכמה כהולכה בשבילים ישרים, שבהם הדרך אינה נעשית צרה והריצה אינה מסתיימת במכשול. הקריאה חותמת בדרישה להחזיק במוסר כחיים עצמם, ולא ללכת בדרך הרשעים או לקנא בדרכם של עושי רעה.
explanation.en: The father asks his son to listen and receive from him, linking this with an increase in the years of his life. He describes instruction in wisdom as guidance along upright paths, where the way is not constricted and running does not end in a stumble. The reading closes by calling for a firm hold on discipline as life itself, and for neither walking in the wicked path nor envying the way of evil people.

dayTitle.en: Holding Fast to the Words and Embracing Wisdom

explanation.he: הקריאה פותחת בהוראה לאחוז בדברים בלב, לשמור את המצוות ולחיות. בנוסח הפתיחה מופיע ‘(יְיָ)’ בלי שזיקתו התחבירית מפורשת. החכמה והבינה מוצגות כקניין שיש לבקש ולזכור; אין לנטוש את החכמה או לסטות מן הדברים שנאמרו. החכמה מתוארת בלשון נקבה: היא שומרת, בוחרת באוהב אותה, מרוממת ומכבדת את הדבק בה, ומניחה יופי וכתר על ראשו.
explanation.en: The reading opens with an instruction to hold the words in the heart, keep the commandments, and live. The supplied opening includes ‘(יְיָ)’ without making its grammatical attachment explicit. Wisdom and understanding are presented as acquisitions to seek and remember; wisdom must not be abandoned, nor should one turn aside from the sayings. Wisdom is personified as feminine: she guards, chooses the person who loves her, raises up and honors the one who holds to her, and places beauty and a crown upon that person's head.

dayTitle.en: Honor for the Wise and Attention to a Father’s Discipline

explanation.he: הקריאה מציבה את סחיפת המלגלגים מול החסד הניתן לענווים, ואת ירושת הכבוד של החכמים מול הקלון שמקבלים הכסילים. אחר כך היא קוראת לבנים להקשיב למוסר אב, ללמוד בינה ולא לנטוש את ההוראה הטובה שניתנה להם. הדובר מסיים בתיאור עצמו כבן לאביו, מפונק ויחיד לפני אמו.
explanation.en: The reading contrasts the sweeping away of scoffers with kindness given to the humble, and the wise inheriting honor with fools receiving disgrace. It then calls on sons to listen to a father’s discipline, learn understanding, and not abandon the good instruction given to them. The speaker closes by describing himself as a son to his father, tenderly cherished and an only son before his mother.
